```{r graph 1 -spaghetti pct change}
# rates over time, need to set a factor order for the rate_yr, OR map them to years. 
#will now try group by property number then calculate the year on year percentage change, 

graph_1_data <- wdc_rates %>%
  arrange(property_no, rate_yr) %>%
  group_by(property_no) %>%
  mutate(pct_change = (`total rates` - lag(`total rates`)) / lag(`total rates`) * 100,
         pct_change = replace_na(pct_change, 0)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(property_no, rate_yr, `total rates`, pct_change) %>%
  filter(property_no != 6318) #remove outlier

graph_1_summary <- graph_1_data %>% 
  group_by(rate_yr) %>%
  summarise(median_pct = median(pct_change),
            mean_pct = mean(pct_change),
            .groups = 'drop')
  
#spaghetti plot
#property 6318 has a 13464.58% rates change. That is odd. I will drop it. A commerical property that was increasedd from42 to 5710 in 24_25
graph_1 <- graph_1_data %>% 
ggplot(aes(x = rate_yr, y = pct_change, group = property_no)) +
  geom_line(col = "#6190F7", alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_line(data = graph_1_summary, aes(x = rate_yr, y = median_pct, group = 1), col = "#DC0100", linewidth = 1) +
  theme(legend.position = 'none')

# I think this is pretty good for a start, maybe trim out more outliers so audience can see the pct change around the median.
```
